Scope: Historical primary-source research and limitations; no implementation copied or changed.

Sources.title: Ctrl-C doesn't work in PowerShell and cmd
Sources.supports: Original report names Windows 7 Enterprise SP1 x64 and failure to abort CMD/PowerShell input.
Sources.limit: Historical matching symptom, not evidence of the current selection race.

Sources.title: Freeze behavior on inactive console buffers
Sources.supports: Maintainer reports Windows 7 selection blocks writes to inactive buffers, for both Mark and SelectAll.
Sources.limit: Protective output synchronization must be retained; this test does not measure cancellation.

Sources.title: Mark alternative reverted
Sources.supports: Maintainer reports cursor interference and screen corruption from the Mark alternative.
Sources.limit: Do not substitute Mark as an assumed solution.

Sources.title: GUI Ctrl+C implementation
Sources.supports: Upstream tried window messages for prompt cancellation.

Sources.title: Revert GUI processed Ctrl+C
Sources.limit: Historical design decision does not establish impossibility of a verified in-host operation.

Sources.title: Maintainer analysis of background keyboards, ordering and NUL
Sources.supports: Explains modifier-state problems across background desktops, unsafe global input, queued-message reordering and NUL character records from synchronous sends.
Sources.limit: Current nested modifier traces address one observed boundary; selection and raw-character fidelity remain separate.

Sources.title: GUI unprocessed Ctrl+C produces NUL
Sources.supports: Maintainer records NUL characters and a PowerShell failure on the unprocessed GUI path.
Sources.limit: The diagnostic Character=0 contract is not equivalent to the accepted unprocessed transport's character 0x03.

Sources.title: Initial Windows 7 GUI cancellation result
Sources.supports: Maintainer reports prompt cancellation working for CMD and PowerShell on Windows 7 before the broader limitations were found.
Sources.limit: Plausibility, not a qualification of the current implementation.

Sources.title: Different types of input can be reordered
Sources.supports: Input-record batching must be flushed before a separately issued event or window message.
Sources.limit: Historical input-ordering hazard, not measured as the cause of the current two traced failures.

Sources.title: ConEmu processed Ctrl+C input path
Sources.supports: Uses a window key message for processed Ctrl+C, cites issue 590, warns about modifiers.
Sources.limit: Its readiness checks do not prove a solution to this exact scrape-freeze race.

Sources.title: ConEmu output pause and selection
Sources.supports: Pauses through Mark, resumes with Escape, and treats selection as halted output.

Sources.title: Compatibility implementation of selection key handling
Sources.supports: Active-selection branch clears selection on Ctrl+C/Escape and returns before ordinary input; SelectAll sets mouse-style selection.
Sources.limit: Independent compatibility implementation, not Windows 7 source. Its selection branch filters non-WM_KEYDOWN messages, so it does not establish WinPTY WM_CHAR Escape behavior. Behavioral reference only; no code copied.

Sources.title: Console improvements in Windows 10 Technical Preview
Sources.supports: Microsoft presents the newer dual copy/cancel Ctrl+C keyboard behavior as a Windows 10 console change.
Sources.limit: Do not infer that Windows 7 follows current copy-to-clipboard behavior.

Sources.title: SetConsoleMode
Sources.supports: QuickEdit is bit 0x40 and can be disabled using extended flags; processed input is a separate flag.
Sources.limit: Disabling QuickEdit does not prevent the agent from explicitly invoking SelectAll.

Sources.title: CONSOLE_SELECTION_INFO
Sources.supports: Flags 7 combine selection in progress, nonempty selection, and mouse-style selection.
Sources.limit: The flags do not identify which process caused selection or establish atomic state at key entry.

Sources.title: SendMessage
Sources.supports: Synchronous cross-thread sending blocks and can process incoming nonqueued messages while waiting.
Sources.limit: A coordination handshake inside the host callback can introduce circular waits.
